hints: Focus on what functional groups are present in X and what Fehling's solution actually tests for.
X contains both a secondary alcohol and an aldehyde, so think about what each becomes with excess hot acidified dichromate under reflux.
Compare the functional groups in X and in the fully oxidised product Y, then decide which one still has the group that reduces Fehling's to a red precipitate.
walkthrough:
**Spot the groups in X**

Look carefully at the structure. X is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO}$ which is 3-hydroxy-2-methylbutanal.

It has two oxidisable groups: a secondary alcohol ($\text{-CH(OH)-}$) and an aldehyde ($\text{-CHO}$).

**Oxidise strongly to get Y**

Excess acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ under reflux is vigorous oxidation, so it oxidises everything it can.

Secondary alcohol to ketone and aldehyde to carboxylic acid:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH(CH}_3\text{)CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH(CH}_3\text{)COOH}$$
So Y is a keto-acid with no aldehyde left.

**Apply the Fehling's test rule**

Fehling's solution warmed gives a brick-red precipitate of $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ only with aliphatic aldehydes. It does not react with ketones, carboxylic acids or alcohols.

X still has $\text{-CHO}$, so positive. Y has only ketone and acid, so negative. Therefore only X gives the red precipitate.

options.A: Incorrect. Y no longer contains an aldehyde after strong oxidation, it contains a ketone and a carboxylic acid, neither of which reduces Fehling's solution.
options.B: Correct. X contains an aldehyde group so it reduces Fehling's to red Cu2O. Y is CH3COCH(CH3)COOH after both groups are oxidised, so it has no aldehyde and gives no precipitate.
options.C: Incorrect and backwards. It is X that has the aldehyde. Y has lost its aldehyde by oxidation to a carboxylic acid, so Y cannot be the positive one.
options.D: Incorrect. This would ignore the aldehyde in X. Any aliphatic aldehyde warmed with Fehling's gives the red precipitate, so X must be positive.
